title: workflow-hardening lint and job rule: reviewer items 3, 5 and 6-10 on #246
description: Source: the Opus reviewer unit on opum-ai/opum-marketplace#246 at head f44a0fa (REQUEST CHANGES; blocking item and items 1-4 fixed in the follow-up commit), relayed by the leader. NOT in #246. (3) LINT: scan the whole run text for any ignore[-_]scripts and allow only a bare or =true value; also inline env assignment, export, unset, env -u and writes to $GITHUB_ENV, since a CLI flag or those forms outrank the job variable. (5) SCOPE: require the variable on EVERY job in every workflow, which closes the class for jobs the detector cannot recognise as npm jobs. Item 5 changes the rule scope, so it goes to opum-doc for a decision before anyone builds it. (6-10) jobBlocks layout and anchor blind spots in scripts/test/workflow-hardening.test.mjs (the reviewer relayed ids only; read the verdict for the specifics). implementationNotes: REVIEWER SPECIFICS for #246 at f44a0fa (Opus unit, relayed by the leader; relay wording, not the reviewer record). ITEM 3: npm ranks CLI flags above env, so `npm update --no-ignore-scripts` or `npm link --ignore-scripts=false` turns scripts back on, and NPM_CMD does not list those subcommands. Also unseen: inline `npm_config_ignore_scripts=false npm ...`, export / unset / env -u, and `echo ... >> $GITHUB_ENV` (IGNORE_ENV needs `key:`). Cheap fix: scan the whole run text for any ignore[-_]scripts occurrence and allow only bare or true values. ITEM 5 (scope, to opum-doc first): the job rule covers only jobs recognised as npm jobs (NPM_CMD or setup-node). A new ubuntu-latest job (npm preinstalled) with no setup-node and `run: npm update`, `/usr/bin/npm link`, or a script file that calls npm passes both rules. Proposed: require the variable on EVERY job (2 lines in promotion-guards.yml). ITEM 6: a quoted (`  "b":`) or commented (`  b: # x`) job key does not split the job, so its lines join the previous job and borrow its jobTrue; coveredJobs===3 counts blocks, so it does not catch this. ITEM 7: a column-0 `#` comment inside a job ends the block, so later steps belong to no job. ITEM 8: `jobs: # x` or a 4-space job indent returns [] with no violation; jobsRead>=5 is a total across files, so a new file can escape; a top-level key after jobs: (e.g. `on:` with `  push:`) reads as a bogus job. ITEM 9: the opt-out scan reads only job blocks; a top-level anchor (`env: &off` holding false) reused as a step `env: *off` overrides the job true unseen; refusing `*alias` and `<<:` in workflows closes it. ITEM 10: a block-scalar value under job env: containing the text `npm_config_ignore_scripts: "true"` satisfies jobTrue.

TWO NOTES from the #246 confirmatory round. (a) Arm 3 of scripts/test/install-ignore-scripts.test.sh on npm 12 now passes --dangerously-allow-all-scripts together with npm_config_ignore_scripts=true. These are different config keys, so which one wins is npm own logic. Either way the arm is sound (a real proof, or a loud true red), but record the outcome the first time anyone runs it on npm 12. (b) The ci.yml comment calling the line lint "the backstop" for --no-ignore-scripts / --ignore-scripts=false is only true for the subcommands NPM_CMD lists; it belongs with item 3.

GOVERNING RECORD, DEC-277 (a1), opum-doc 2026-11-17, relayed by the leader VERBATIM. Item 5 is decided; this note supersedes "job level on jobs that run npm" in DEC-277 (ii) and OMARK-109, and the job-to-workflow-level move may be folded into this task. NOT STARTED: this task is not in the approved plan; a new item waits for a plan approval.

--- DEC-277 (a1), verbatim ---
The rule:
1. Every workflow sets `npm_config_ignore_scripts: "true"` once, in its WORKFLOW-level `env:`. Every job and step inherits it, so the protection doesn't depend on recognising npm at all. That's one line per workflow rather than one per job.
2. The lint changes from "recognised npm jobs carry it" to two checks:
   (a) every workflow file has the top-level env entry, exactly "true";
   (b) no job-level or step-level `env:` sets npm_config_ignore_scripts to anything else.
3. The only exception is DEC-277's explicit opt-out: a job that genuinely needs lifecycle scripts may override it, but only with an adjacent `# ignore-scripts-opt-out: <reason>` comment. The lint accepts an override only with that comment and lists every opt-out in its output.
4. The old command-recognition rule stays as a backstop, as before.

PROOF:
- a new ubuntu-latest job with no setup-node, running `npm update`, `/usr/bin/npm link` or a script that calls npm, is covered by inheritance;
- a workflow missing the top-level entry fails;
- a job overriding it to "false" without the comment fails, and with the comment passes and is listed;
- mutation control: dropping check (b) makes exactly the silent-override case pass.
--- end ---
Note from the leader: point 3's opt-out marker (`# ignore-scripts-opt-out: <reason>`) replaces OMARK-109's `opt-out reason:` comment plus pinned OPT_OUTS list; when OMARK-111 is built, that is part of the change. It is DEC-182 floor work (CI workflow plus required-check logic), so it gets a floor run and an Opus review.

DELIVERED per DEC-277 (a1). ci.yml and promotion-guards.yml set npm_config_ignore_scripts: "true" ONCE in the workflow-level env (the three ci.yml job-level blocks from OMARK-109 are removed). workflow-hardening.test.mjs: workflowEnvViolations = (a) every workflow has the top-level entry, exactly "true", read at the env block own child indent (item 10); (b) any job or step override is refused unless the line directly above is `# ignore-scripts-opt-out: <reason>` (replaces OMARK-109 OPT_OUTS and `opt-out reason:`); accepted opt-outs are LISTED in the suite output (workflowOptOuts, 0 today, asserted). Item 3: every run: line is scanned for any override flag (--no-ignore-scripts, --ignore-scripts=false, on ANY subcommand) and any touch of the variable other than a plain =true assignment (inline env, export, unset, env -u, GITHUB_ENV). Items 6-10: jobBlocks accepts quoted keys and trailing comments (6), a column-0 comment does not end a job (7), `jobs: # x`/4-space jobs report "no jobs were read" and a top-level key ends the jobs region (8), anchors, aliases and <<: are refused (9). Old command-recognition rule kept as the backstop. PROOF: 28 rejecting and 9 accepting fixtures including the ruling cases (a new job with no setup-node running npm update, /usr/bin/npm link or a script calling npm is covered by inheritance; a workflow missing the entry fails; a job overriding to "false" fails without the comment, passes with it and is listed). MUTATION: dropping check (b) turned exactly the 9 silent-override fixtures red (job/step false, non-adjacent comment, empty reason, hyphen spelling, empty value, quoted-key job, trailing-comment job key, column-0-comment job); dropping check (a) turned exactly the 3 missing-entry fixtures red; indent-any-level for the top env turned exactly the item-10 fixture red; dropping the whole-run-text flag scan turned exactly the 2 unlisted-subcommand fixtures red; widening adjacency to 3 lines turned exactly the not-adjacent fixture red. NOT DONE / unmeasured: the arm-3 outcome on npm 12 (record it the first time it runs there); the leader item (b) comment now says the lint catches an override flag on any subcommand. Suites: workflow-hardening 133, others unchanged.

CORRECTION to the DELIVERED note: the fixture counts are 24 rejecting and 9 accepting (not 28), measured by counting the suite output lines. The mutation results listed there (9, 3, 1, 2, 1 red) were read from the runs.

REOPENED 2026-11-18 for the #249 fix round: round 1 review (opus unit, head 8a034bc) found B1-B4 blocking, so AC3 (each proven both ways) is unmet. Title no longer says (not started) (N3). N1 stays with opum-doc.

ROUND 2 (opus unit on cf187bf: CHANGES; B4 closed, B1-B3 each had a remaining bypass) FIXED IN ROUND 3, items 1-10 of the verdict. AC1 (item 3 override forms) is UNCHECKED: round-1 B1/B3 and round-2 items 3 and 4 are item-3 forms, so the reopen note attributing B1-B4 to AC3 only was incomplete. FIXED: (1) env: with a dash prefix, quoted or plain scalar value, block scalar, or a value on the next line is refused unless it is a block mapping; (2) a double-quoted scalar containing a backslash outside block-scalar bodies is refused (YAML decodes escapes in keys and values); (3) IGNORE_ENV needs whitespace before a comment, so a stuck # is part of the value; (4a) any option-like token whose name is a prefix (2+ chars) of ignore-scripts, with dashes, no- runs, case and = value ignored, is an occurrence, so --ignore=false IS now closed; (4b) quotes and backslashes are deleted from a token before both the flag and the variable-name matches; (4c) the flag scan covers every non-comment line of the file, not only run text; (4d) logical lines join across a backslash-newline with nothing between. (6) env -i, env -, env --ignore-environment and BASH_ENV are refused; (7) npm 12 --dangerously-allow-all-scripts and its npm_config_ form are refused in workflows (which wins on npm 12 is UNMEASURED); (8)(9)(10) stale arm-3 text fixed, the three-dash fixture is labelled a regression guard, and the suite goes red if .github/actions exists. MUTATION (each on a copy of the suite): dropping the optional env dash 2 red; env next-line check off 1 red; both value refusals off 7 red (the non-empty-value refusal alone is 0 red, it overlaps the next-line check); escape rule off 3; old IGNORE_ENV comment rule 1; no prefix match 4; deq identity 5 (3 of them accepting-side); flag scan limited to run: lines 3; logical-line join with a space 1 (after the 4d fixture was reworked, since the first version was caught by the abbreviation rule and did not discriminate); env -i check off 3; BASH_ENV off 1; allow-all off 2; escape rule inside block bodies 3 accepting-side red; always-refuse env 51 red; variableTouches without deq 2; creating .github/actions turns the suite red. DECLINED RESIDUALS, with reasons (a line scanner is the design, a parser is a dependency under DEC-182 (1)): a flag or variable name the shell assembles at run time ($A$B, eval, indirect expansion); anything inside a script file or a local composite action (never opened; item 10 makes the suite red if .github/actions appears); sudo npm (Ubuntu env_reset drops the variable, UNMEASURED on the runner, not refused); which of --dangerously-allow-all-scripts and ignore-scripts wins on npm 12 (UNMEASURED, refused outright instead). N4/N5 GAP RECORD: the lint cannot see a YAML anchor reaching a value in a form this reader does not scan beyond the refusals above, a multi-line double-quoted scalar without a backslash split, or any env set outside the workflow file (repository or organisation variables feeding env through an expression is refused only where the env: key itself is an expression). N1 (optOutsListed === 0) stays with opum-doc.

ROUND 3 NOTE (appended; the earlier N4/N5 GAP RECORD entry is left as written and is CORRECTED here). Round 3 review (opus unit on e5400c0): CHANGES. Fixed in the next commit: B1 a comment line or an escaped backslash at line end no longer hides the next line (every physical line is scanned as well as the joined logical line; a comment is never extended; only an odd run of backslashes continues); B2 the value word after a bare --ignore-scripts is read with quotes and backslashes deleted (fa then quoted lse, fals then backslash e). Mutation: the old joining (no physical lines, comments extended, any backslash a continuation) turns the three B1 fixtures red; reading the value word raw turns the three B2 fixtures red; the physical-line scan alone discriminates, the odd-run and no-comment-extension rules are belt and braces (0 red alone). CORRECTIONS to the earlier N4/N5 entry: (1) N4 verbatim text is: env-stripping commands (sudo npm update, env -i, docker run), script files called from run:, remote reusable workflows (no env inheritance). To the declined or recorded list ADD docker run (env-stripping) and remote reusable workflows (jobs.x.uses: owner/repo/path@ref, which do not inherit the caller workflow env). env -i is refused; sudo npm update and docker run are recorded not refused. (2) N5 (the five variable-tampering fixtures) is accepted as-is (unique needle) and was not individually mutation-checked; emptying variableTouches turned them red together with others, but no per-fixture check was made. (3) The earlier phrase refused only where the env: key itself is an expression read as a decline of a closable form. It was not a decision: an env value reaching npm through repository or organisation variables via an expression is refused at the env: key and is not otherwise visible, and no decline of any closable form was intended. HELD for opum-doc scope ruling (leader relay): B3 YAML folds, B4 multi-line double-quoted escapes, B5 brace expansion and dollar-quote forms, B6 expression, alias and explicit-key forms, and N1-N5 of round 3. AC1 and AC3 stay unchecked.

ROUND 4 (DEC-277 (a2), opum-doc, recorded under ODOC-605 in opum-ai/opum-doc#1773; relayed by the leader VERBATIM): "2. OMARK-111 N1, DEC-277 (a2) Q1: A. Drop the optOutsListed === 0 assertion. A commented opt-out passes and is listed in the suite output, as (a1) point 3 says. The second look comes from the DEC-183 review every workflow change already gets. 3. OMARK-111 lint scope, DEC-277 (a2) Q2: A, exactly as proposed. YAML side: a strict layout allowlist (| bodies only; single-line scalars elsewhere; no > folds or plain-scalar continuations; no backslash outside bodies; no anchors, aliases, ? keys or expression keys). Shell side: closes only the structural forms (brace groups, $ then quote forms in option-like or variable-naming tokens, and the de-quoted value word after --ignore-scripts). The lint declines by name all shell expansion and quoting deq does not model, any interpreter assembling the name, env-clearing commands (sudo, su -, exec -c, setpriv, docker run/exec, ssh), remote reusable workflows, and local or third-party actions. The stated claim, in the comments and the OMARK-111 record: catches plain-text and accidental overrides of the workflow-level protection; not a defence against an adversarial workflow author. The writer re-triages B3-B6 and N1-N5 against that contract: fix what is inside it, decline by name what is outside. Round 4 is reviewed against the contract, not against every spelling." STATED CLAIM (verbatim, also in the test header, ci.yml and promotion-guards.yml comments): "catches plain-text and accidental overrides of the workflow-level protection; not a defence against an adversarial workflow author". ROUND 4 TRIAGE: B3 YAML folds = FIXED (a > folded scalar and a plain-scalar continuation are refused). B4 multi-line double-quoted escapes = FIXED (any backslash outside a | body is refused; a quoted scalar must close on its own line). B5 brace expansion, dollar-single-quote and dollar-double-quote = FIXED for option-like and variable-naming tokens (brace groups with a comma or .., and dollar-quote forms); DECLINED BY NAME in any other token, and all other shell expansion and quoting deq does not model. B6 expression, alias and ? keys = FIXED (aliases were already refused; ? keys and expression keys now refused; env: with an expression value was refused in round 3). N1 (optOutsListed === 0) = FIXED by dropping the assertion per Q1; a commented opt-out passes and is listed. N2-N5 of round 3: triage follows when the reviewer text is in hand. DECLINED BY NAME: all shell expansion and quoting deq does not model; any interpreter assembling the name; env-clearing commands (sudo, su -, exec -c, setpriv, docker run/exec, ssh); remote reusable workflows; local or third-party actions (a suite tripwire fires only if .github/actions appears); the npm 12 precedence question (UNMEASURED; the flag is refused outright). AC1 and AC3 stay unchecked until the round-4 review.

ROUND 4 TRIAGE, round-3 reviewer text (opus unit on e5400c0) against the (a2) contract. B3 YAML folds = FIXED (a > fold and a plain-scalar continuation are refused). B4 multi-line double-quoted escapes = FIXED (any backslash outside a | body is refused, and a quoted scalar must close on its own line; the reviewer fixture is a rejecting case). The earlier phrase about a multi-line double-quoted scalar without a backslash split was never a decline: it is closed (multi-line quoted scalars are refused). B5 = FIXED for brace groups (comma or ..) and the dollar-single-quote and dollar-double-quote forms in option-like or variable-naming tokens, including a token that begins with those quote forms (it can hide the dash), and a brace group inside npm_config_ names; DECLINED BY NAME: a brace group that builds a command word such as {env,-i} (env-clearing commands class) and all other expansion deq does not model. B6 = FIXED: expression keys at any key position, any anchor or alias at a key or value position outside bodies, and ? explicit keys are refused; item 9 of the earlier list is therefore true as now implemented. N1 (round 3) = DECLINED BY NAME as a class, per the round-1 record-do-not-chase ruling: any command or builtin that starts a child with a fresh or altered environment (env long-option spellings and abbreviations, env -S, sudo, su -, exec -c, setpriv --reset-env, docker run/exec, ssh); the cheap exact fix was made (BASH_ENV is tested on the de-quoted line). N2 = FIXED: --dangerously-allow-all-scripts is refused by full name and by option-name prefix of 4 or more characters (whether npm 12 still expands abbreviations is UNMEASURED; refusing costs nothing on the real workflows). N3 = FIXED (comment now says the joining regex removes the next line indentation, over-joining, stricter than bash). N4 = FIXED: a step uses: ./path is refused except ./.github/workflows/; the .github/actions tripwire stays. Third-party actions that call core.exportVariable for later steps are a trust class this lint cannot cover: DECLINED BY NAME (local or third-party actions). N5 = FIXED (declined-list wording widened to any interpreter: the shell, node -e, github-script core.exportVariable with a concatenated name). MUTATION for this commit: naming test narrowed 1 red; dollar-quote start not option-like 1; BASH_ENV on the raw line 1; expression-key rule off 2; anchor-alias rule off 1; local-action rule off 1, and refusing workflows too 1 (accepting side); allow-all prefix rule off 1; its 4-character floor lowered to 1 turns the one-letter accepting fixture red.
